page: Microsoft Azure E2_v3 is an entry-level memory-optimized virtual machine from the Ev3 family. It runs on the x86_64 architecture using a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor. This configuration provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The processor features a 50 MB L3 cache and supports hardware-assisted virtualization via Intel VMX, alongside AVX, AES, and FMA instruction sets.

The server is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It includes 51 GB of local SSD storage. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are bundled with this instance, and it does not feature any GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks place the E2_v3 in the lower tier of cloud instances. Stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, along with Geekbench and PassMark CPU scores, consistently rank in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with uncached read speeds at 9.34 GB/sec and write speeds at 6.41 GB/sec. Similarly, database operations, Redis SET performance at 1.09 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput at 1.3 GB/sec reflect its constrained compute and memory throughput capabilities.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E2_v3 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring a larger memory footprint relative to compute power. However, the tradeoff is significantly reduced processing speed and memory bandwidth. It is best suited for lightweight memory-intensive applications, small databases, development environments, or basic caching layers that do not demand high CPU throughput.
